scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Licensed or registered where you live (check your country's financial regulator)
Large and long-established, with a good security record
Supports your bank's deposit method and the coins/networks you'll use (ETH, USDC, and…
Unique, long password stored in a password manager (e.g. Bitwarden, 1Password)
Secure your email first
scenes.vo: An exchange is a company that lets you swap your normal money (dollars, pounds, euros) for crypto. It's your on-ramp. Choose one that is: Well-known examples include Coinbase, Kraken, Binance, Bybit and OKX, but availability differs by country. Pick one that's legally available to you. You'll be asked for K.Y.C. ("know your customer"): ID and sometimes proof of address. This is normal and legally required for regulated exchanges. Secure it before depositing: First, Licensed or registered where you live (check your country's financial regulator). Next, Large and long-established, with a good security record. Then, Supports your bank's deposit method and the coins/networks you'll use (ETH, U.S.D.C., and low-cost networks such as Arbitrum or Base). Also, Unique, long password stored in a password manager (for example Bitwarden, 1Password). On top of that, Secure your email first. Whoever controls your email can often reset your exchange account. Give it its own strong password and two-factor.

You'll be asked for KYC ("know your customer"): ID and sometimes proof of address. This is normal and legally required for regulated exchanges. Secure it before depositing: First, Licensed or registered where you live (check your country's financial regulator). Next, Large and long-established, with a good security record. Then, Supports your bank's deposit method and the coins/networks you'll use (ETH, USDC, and low-cost networks such as Arbitrum or Base). Also, Unique, long password stored in a password manager (e.g. Bitwarden, 1Password). On top of that, Secure your email first. Whoever controls your email can often reset your exchange account. Give it its own strong password and 2FA.

scenes.title: Key ideas (cont.)
items: Two-factor authentication (2FA) with an authenticator app (e.g. Google Authenticator,…
Save the 2FA backup codes offline (on paper, stored safely)
Turn on the anti-phishing code if offered (a word that appears in every real email from…
Turn on the withdrawal address allowlist if offered (withdrawals can only go to…
scenes.vo: And Two-factor authentication (two-factor) with an authenticator app (for example Google Authenticator, Authy) or a hardware security key. Avoid SMS codes: phone numbers can be hijacked ("SIM swap"). Plus, Save the two-factor backup codes offline (on paper, stored safely). One more: Turn on the anti-phishing code if offered (a word that appears in every real email from the exchange). And finally, Turn on the withdrawal address allowlist if offered (withdrawals can only go to addresses you pre-approved).

scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. Maria signs up, completes K.Y.C. in 10 minutes, then spends another 10 on security: password manager, authenticator-app two-factor on both her email and the exchange, backup codes on paper, and an anti-phishing code "blue-kettle". Later, an email arrives about a "suspicious login" with no "blue-kettle" in it. She knows it's fake and deletes it.

KYC complete
Email secured with its own strong password + 2FA
Exchange 2FA via authenticator app or security key (not SMS)
Backup codes stored offline

scenes.q: Why secure your email before the exchange?
scenes.a: Email is often how accounts are reset. Whoever controls it can take over the exchange account.
